reason: Verified verbatim against the running master, not inferred. lately.html:498 defines plural(n, one, many) — the mechanism for agreement exists and is used at lines 525, 550, 620, 628, 636 (including the paired "job has"/"jobs have" in the ages sr line) — but the four kpi() calls at lines 650-653 pass a single fixed word string that is plural-only, and fixture.js sets status.unowned = 1. Driving the surface at file://…/lately.html?v=light&state=full in chromium, the third card's DOM reads exactly "1" + "have nobody's name on them" and its .sr accessible name reads exactly "1 job have nobody's name on them, of 9 jobs open"; the same string appears in state=partial. In state=quiet the sentence at lately.html:758 renders exactly "All 9 open jobs has moved inside a fortnight, none is past its day, and every one has a name on it." Both quotes in the finding are character-for-character correct. Not covered by either gate: audit.mjs checks palette, weights, families, contrast, hit targets, radii, motion and type ramp, interaction-check.mjs checks behaviour, and neither parses copy — so this is not a restatement of anything already proven. Not in lessons.md either; the nearest entry ("One grammar per fact") is about mixed date grammars, a different class. The fix is copy-only: no colour, no weight, no metric, no architecture, so no non-negotiable is touched, and the pairing mechanism is exactly the one the file already uses elsewhere. Two accuracy corrections that do not change the verdict: (1) the quiet sentence is below the 960px fold in shots/light-quiet--1440x960.png — it is in the shipped quiet state and renders on scroll, but it is not literally visible in that frame, so "both are in the shipped frames" is loose; (2) three of the four proposed pairs are right, but "are past the day they were due" adds a verb to a label that currently ships without one and is currently correct — see sharpenedFix. Severity is correctly classed: the counts are right, so nothing untrue is asserted (not misleading) and the surface still does what it says (not blocking); it is visibly wrong but passable. Defect stands.
sharpenedFix: Change kpi()'s `word` to a pair `{ one, many }` and select with the existing plural() spirit — `const w = n === 1 ? word.one : word.many` — so n = 0 keeps taking the many form, which is already correct today ("0 jobs are waiting on something else"). Use: still — "hasn't moved in a fortnight" / "haven't moved in a fortnight"; nobody — "has nobody's name on it" / "have nobody's name on them"; waiting — "is waiting on something else" / "are waiting on something else". For overdue, do NOT adopt the seat's "are past the day they were due": keep the shipped label byte-identical at "past the day they were due" and pair it with "past the day it was due", so the only string that changes is the one that is currently wrong. Two things the seat's fix leaves unspecified and must be handled: the `unavailable` branch at lately.html:527 builds `${word}: not available…` where the count is unknown by definition — it must take `word.many` explicitly, or it will throw on an object; and the visible label span at line 532 must render the same selected `w` that the .sr name uses, or the card and its accessible name diverge, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. For the quiet sentence at line 758, do not hard-code "have": build it from the same selection so it agrees at any denominator — "All 9 open jobs have moved inside a fortnight" at n > 1 and "The one open job has moved inside a fortnight" at n = 1, since "All 1 open job have/has moved" is awkward either way. The remainder of that sentence ("none is past its day, and every one has a name on it") is already correct and must not be touched.
breaks: Copy-only, so nothing structural is at risk, but four things must be re-measured after it lands. (1) Label width: the singular strings are within a character or two of the plurals, so the 5-across grid holds — but if the seat's "are past the day they were due" is taken instead, card 2's label grows by four characters and that card is the tightest in the row; re-shoot 1280x900 and 1440x960 and the 2-across breakpoint at 768 and 390 (.kpis goes to repeat(2, 1fr) at the 437 media query, with .kpi.lead spanning both) and confirm no label wraps to a third line and the meter baseline stays aligned across all five cards. (2) The accessible names change, so re-run interaction-check.mjs — any assertion matching on the old "1 job have nobody's name on them" or on the quiet sentence will fail on the new string and needs updating in the same commit, not silenced. (3) Re-run audit.mjs for leading and type-ramp on .t-small if any label gains a line. (4) Guard the honest-degradation contract: after the pair lands, re-drive state=partial and confirm the overdue card still reads "— / past the day they were due / Not available" with the sr name "past the day they were due: not available, because Timeline did not answer" — passing an object where a string was is the exact way that branch renders "[object Object]" and silently breaks a protected object. Also re-drive state=quiet and first-run, which both reuse these strings.
